html:
On 20 September 1906 Dutch troops landed in south Bali and marched on Denpasar, capital of the kingdom of Badung. The king, his court and their families, dressed in white, walked out to face the guns in a puputan, a ritual fight to the death.

Hundreds were killed. The king of Tabanan was captured and killed himself, and another puputan followed at Klungkung in 1908, completing the Dutch conquest of the island.

The news shocked Europe. Dutch rule then preserved Bali's Hindu culture, a legacy of Majapahit, as a tourist draw. Denpasar's main square has a monument to the puputan. See Netherlands.
